title: Per-customer & per-route optimization policies: segmentation, allowlists/denylists, and safe apply/rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Add a per-customer and per-route layer to Redwood's cost-optimization automation so batching and caching recommendations (and their automatic application) can be scoped by segmentation, allowlists/denylists, and customer tiers. We must also provide a safe apply/rollback mechanism that supports canaries, dry-runs, and auditability.
background: We already generate per-route batching/caching suggestions from workload analysis (see ENG-7312). Customers and internal teams have asked for finer-grained controls: some customers (enterprise or regulated) cannot use aggressive caching or shared KV caches, while others (low-latency frontend routes) require minimized batching. Additionally, when automatically applying configuration changes we need safe rollback and observability to avoid customer regressions and to comply with audit requirements.
acceptance_criteria: Policy model: implement a policy schema that supports segmentation by customer_id, route pattern, and customer_tier with allowlist/denylist rules
UI: Console page where operators can view existing policies, preview matching routes/customers, and create new policies with priority order
API: CRUD endpoints for policies with validation and dry-run mode
Recommendation engine: recommendations can be filtered/masked by policy before being surfaced or automatically applied
Safe apply: support staged rollout (canary percent by customer or route tag), automatic rollback on defined regression signals (latency/P95 error rate/cost delta), and manual abort
Audit logs: every automated change must emit an immutable audit event with diff, trigger (rule/recommendation), and outcome
Metrics & alerts: per-policy KPIs (applied-savings, estimated-cost-savings, regression-incidents) visible in Console and alertable
E2E tests: coverage for policy matching, dry-run behavior, canary progression, and rollback triggers
tasks: Design policy schema (proto/jsonschema) and storage model: support priority and combinators
Extend recommendation pipeline to evaluate policies and emit filtered candidate set
Implement policy evaluation engine in runtime control-plane (low-latency matching)
Build Console CRUD UI and preview modal for affected customers/routes
Wire safe-apply orchestration: canary controller, health checks, rollback hook
Integrate audit logging with existing audit sink (Kafka -> S3/WORM) and surface in Console
Add observability: per-policy Prometheus metrics, Grafana dashboards, and a PagerDuty rule for regressions
Write integration tests and create a staging rollout plan with a small set of beta customers
notes: Policy examples: allowlist customers with tag 'trusted' to get KV caching=aggressive; denylist 'pci' customers from any shared-kv caching; route pattern '/user/*/inbox' set batch_max=8 for premium tier
Priority semantics: higher-priority policies override lower ones; explicit deny wins over allow when priority equal
Edge cases: multi-tenant routes where a single route maps to multiple customers (we must evaluate per-customer per-request) — this will influence runtime matching approach
Fallback behavior: if a policy blocks an automatic change, recommendation should still appear in Console for manual review unless explicitly suppressed

Rollback signals: primary signals are P95 latency + error-rate + per-customer token cost delta. We will start with conservative thresholds (5% P95 increase OR 0.5% absolute error-rate increase OR cost delta > 20%)
Data privacy: policy preview should not expose PII — previews must show aggregated route/customer counts and examples only
Migration: existing global recommendations will get a default 'global' policy created during rollout to preserve behavior
Timeline constraint: aim to ship policy schema + evaluation + API + small Console UX in runtime-1.20; safe-apply orchestration and broad rollout by runtime-1.21
risks: Incorrect policy matching could either over-apply (customer regressions) or under-apply (lost savings). Need unit + integration tests with synthetic workloads
Complex policy logic may add latency to the hot path; plan to precompile/compile policies into a fast matcher and cache decisions per route/customer pair
Audit and compliance gaps if we fail to retain immutable change records — coordinate with security/compliance
Rollback thrash risk if overly-sensitive signals trigger flip-flop; introduce cooldown windows and require sustained signal before rollback
implementation_decisions: Schema format: JSON Schema for Console/API with a thin proto for internal RPCs
Evaluation location: control-plane will evaluate policy eligibility and produce a per-candidate allow/deny. Runtime will cache decisions and revalidate on policy updates
Canary model: percent-based by matched-entities (customers or route instances). For per-customer rollouts choose customer-count based canaries; for route rollouts choose request-count sampling
Rollback orchestration: use existing rollout controller but extend it with policy-scoped health checks and a non-destructive abort + rollback path
Visibility: every policy change creates an audit event and a Console timeline entry with links to affected deployments/PRs
